title: Konrad Lorenz's birth chart
metaDescription: Konrad Lorenz's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 13.9° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.4° separates Mercury and Neptune from an exact trine; at that range thinking and imagination read as one mechanism. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 13.9° Scorpio, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Jupiter. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 5.3° Scorpio, Venus holds 29.1° Virgo, Mars holds 3.2° Capricorn — in the old shorthand, thought steeped in tone and memory; attraction that grows by reliability; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mercury a third of the circle apart from Neptune, 0.4° off exact. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, the Sun trine Jupiter at 0.4°, and Mercury square Saturn at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, four placements stand out. Venus in Virgo at 29.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Capricorn at 3.2° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Pisces at 13.4° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Aquarius at 3.4° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 4, air 3, earth 2, fire 1, and mutable 5, fixed 3, cardinal 2 across the modes. Water reads the room before the room speaks — atmosphere first, analysis later. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 12.4°.
